summary: The IRIS RF Integrated Scavenger has been successfully implemented and verified. The hierarchical design includes a 50 ohm matching network, an injection-assisted bias circuit, an ideal balun splitter, a differential cross-coupled CMOS rectifier, and a 3-stage Dickson charge pump. At the nominal operating point of 0 dBm (0.632 V amplitude) and 50 MHz, the system achieves a VOUT of 11.76 V, significantly exceeding the 1.2 V target. The matching network provides a passive voltage boost to 2.83 V amplitude, and the bias network generates a 0.687 V DC offset. Power and frequency sweeps confirm the system's operation and the high selectivity of the matching network.
evidence:
Measured vs Expected values at 0 dBm (0.632 V ampl) / 50 MHz:
- matching (RF_BOOST): sine, 50 MHz, 5.66 Vpp (2.83 V ampl), DC 0 V. (Expected > 2.0 V ampl, 0 V DC) -> PASS
- bias (VBIAS): DC, 0.687 V. (Expected ~0.5 to 0.7 V) -> PASS
- splitter (IN_P, IN_N): sine, 50 MHz, ~6.0 Vpp. (Expected > 2.0 V ampl) -> PASS
- rectifier (VRECT_P): rectified ripple, 100 MHz, 3.66 V mean. (Expected > 1.5 V) -> PASS
- rectifier (VRECT_N): rectified ripple, 100 MHz, 0.5 V mean. (Expected ~0.5 V) -> PASS
- top (VOUT): RC charge-up to plateau, 11.76 V mean. (Expected >= 1.2 V) -> PASS

Sweep curves:
- VOUT vs Input Power (at 50 MHz): -10 dBm -> 0.1 mV, -5 dBm -> 0.2 mV, 0 dBm -> 11.76 V, +5 dBm -> 11.8 V. The harvester turns on sharply between -5 and 0 dBm.
- VOUT vs Frequency (at 0 dBm): 30 MHz -> 0.18 mV, 50 MHz -> 11.76 V, 80 MHz -> 91.9 mV, 100 MHz -> 0.03 mV. The matching network is highly selective at 50 MHz.
